categories.main_business_segments: PSEG operates primarily through two main business segments: Public Service Electric and Gas Company (PSE&G), a regulated electric and gas utility in New Jersey, and PSEG Power, which owns and operates merchant nuclear generation assets. Other activities include legacy lease investments, offshore wind interests, and contracted utility operations on Long Island, NY.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: PSE&G's core operations involve electric transmission and distribution (T&D) and natural gas distribution, utilizing advanced grid infrastructure, smart meters, and energy efficiency technologies. PSEG Power operates nuclear power plants using established nuclear generation technology, with a focus on efficient base load operations and robust fuel supply management. The company also invests in regulated solar generation and energy storage pilot projects.
categories.primary_customers_markets: PSE&G serves approximately 2.3 million electric and 1.9 million gas customers, including residential, commercial, and industrial users in New Jersey. PSEG Power sells electricity and capacity into wholesale markets (primarily PJM) and provides gas supply to PSE&G and third parties. The company also manages T&D operations for the Long Island Power Authority under contract.
categories.geographic_coverage: PSEG's primary geographic focus is the Mid-Atlantic United States, especially New Jersey, where it serves about 70% of the state's population. Its nuclear generation assets are located in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, and it has a minority interest in a generation facility in Hawaii. The company also operates the Long Island electric grid under contract.
categories.supply_chain_position: PSE&G operates as a regulated downstream utility, delivering electricity and gas to end users, while PSEG Power functions as a merchant generator (midstream) selling power and capacity into wholesale markets. The company is not involved in upstream fuel extraction but manages fuel procurement and supply for its nuclear fleet.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: PSEG's strategy emphasizes operational excellence, financial strength, and disciplined investment in regulated infrastructure, with a growing focus on clean energy, grid modernization, energy efficiency, and electrification. R&D and investment priorities include smart grid technologies, advanced metering, energy storage, EV infrastructure, and supporting New Jersey's clean energy policy goals. The company targets net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.
categories.revenue_model: PSE&G generates revenue primarily through regulated tariffs for electric transmission and electric/gas distribution, approved by state and federal regulators. PSEG Power earns revenue from wholesale energy, capacity, and ancillary services sales, as well as Zero Emission Certificates (ZECs) and Production Tax Credits (PTCs) for nuclear generation. Additional revenue streams include appliance services, solar generation, and management fees from contracted operations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: PSE&G faces limited direct competition in its regulated utility territory, though it is exposed to evolving regulatory and policy risks. PSEG Power competes with merchant generators, utilities, energy marketers, and new entrants in the PJM and other wholesale markets. The company is a leading utility in New Jersey and a significant nuclear generator in the Mid-Atlantic, with a strong position in regulated T&D and a focus on clean energy leadership.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For 2022, PSEG reported $9.8 billion in operating revenues and $1.03 billion in net income, with PSE&G contributing the majority of earnings. The company has a large asset base ($48.7 billion as of year-end 2022) and a robust capital investment plan ($15.5–$18 billion over 2023–2027). Recent years have seen a shift toward more stable, regulated earnings following the sale of fossil and solar generation assets.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: PSEG emphasizes reliable, safe, and affordable energy delivery, with a growing commitment to clean energy and sustainability. Its value proposition includes industry-leading investments in grid modernization, energy efficiency, and resilience, as well as a strong track record in nuclear generation, which provides the majority of New Jersey's carbon-free electricity. The company differentiates itself through regulatory expertise, operational excellence, and alignment with public policy on decarbonization.
